svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A beaker of water heated from below in the middle."], [1, "Water above the heat source warms up, expands, becomes less dense and rises."], [4, "At the top the warm water spreads out sideways and cools, becoming denser."], [6, "The cooler, denser water sinks at the sides and flows back along the bottom to be heated again."], [9, "This circulation is a convection current. Two loops form here: two convection cells."]]
svg.title: Convection currents
svg.desc: A beaker of water heated in the middle of its base: warm water rises in the centre, spreads, cools and sinks at the sides, forming two convection cells.
svg.text: Red: warmer, less dense water. Blue: cooler, denser water. Dye or particles show the flow.

g.data-info: Particles in liquids and gases can move from place to place, carrying energy with them.
Warms the fluid just above it.
The circulating loop of fluid. Convection only happens in fluids (liquids and gases), not solids. Examples: heating water in a kettle, sea breezes, Earth’s mantle.
Warmed particles move faster and further apart: the fluid expands, becomes less dense and rises.
At the top it spreads out and cools; the particles move closer together, it becomes denser and sinks.
